title: Positive degree is equivalent to ampleness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] (an integral scheme of dimension one, smooth and projective over $k$; in particular proper over $k$) and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $\mathcal L$ is ample on the proper $k$-scheme $X$ in the sense of [def-sc-ample] (some tensor power $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$, $m\geq1$, is very ample) if and only if its degree $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] is positive.

external.place: Varieties, Lemma 0B5X (lemma-ample-curve): 'Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper curve over $k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is ample if and only if $\deg(\mathcal{L}) > 0$.' (The import recorded Tag 01IQ, which is Schemes, Lemma lemma-immersion-when-closed, a fact the blueprint proof uses in passing, not the source of the statement.)

proof.text: *(⇒), the base change.* Assume $\mathcal L$ ample. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X_\Omega:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with projection $p:X_\Omega\to X$ [def-pc-base-change], and $\mathcal L_\Omega:=p^*\mathcal L$ [def-pc-module-pullback], an invertible $\mathcal O_{X_\Omega}$-module. $X$ is proper over $k$ [lem-pc-projective-proper], so $X_\Omega$ is proper over $\Omega$ [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), in particular separated and of finite type; and $X$ is a curve over $k$, so $\dim X_\Omega=1$ [lem-pc-dim-base-change]. Hence $X_\Omega$ is a proper curve over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ of dimension one in the sense of [def-sc-curves] (possibly disconnected).

source.place: proof of the forward direction: the base change XK to K = AlgebraicClosure k, SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 and IsProper by base change, topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension

proof.text: *(⇒), ampleness survives the base change.* By [def-sc-ample] there are $m\geq1$ and a closed immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^N_k$ with $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$. By [lem-pc-very-ample-ample] applied to $i$ and the extension $\Omega/k$, the base change $p^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ is ample on $X_\Omega$, so some power $(p^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes m}))^{\otimes m'}$, $m'\geq1$, is very ample. Pullback commutes with tensor products [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], so $(p^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes m}))^{\otimes m'}\cong\mathcal L_\Omega^{\otimes mm'}$ with $mm'\geq1$; hence $\mathcal L_\Omega$ is ample on $X_\Omega$ [def-sc-ample].

source.place: h.pullback_of_field K, i.e. AlgebraicGeometry.IsAmple.pullback_of_field (Modules/Ample.lean 455-466) from IsVeryAmple.pullback_of_field and Scheme.Modules.nonempty_pullback_tensorPow_iso

proof.text: *(⇒), positivity over $\Omega$.* By [lem-sc-hilbert-polynomial] (the proper $\Omega$-scheme $X_\Omega$ has dimension $1$ and $\mathcal L_\Omega$ is ample invertible by step 2) there is a polynomial $P(n)=an+b$ with $P(n)=\chi(X_\Omega,\mathcal L_\Omega^{\otimes n})$ for all $n\geq0$, and by [lem-sc-ample-positive-degree] (applied to the proper curve $X_\Omega$ of dimension one of step 1 over the algebraically closed $\Omega$) its coefficient of $n$ is positive: $a>0$. Since $\mathcal L_\Omega^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_{X_\Omega}$ and $\mathcal L_\Omega^{\otimes1}=\mathcal L_\Omega$, $b=P(0)=\chi(\mathcal O_{X_\Omega})$ and $a=P(1)-P(0)=\chi(\mathcal L_\Omega)-\chi(\mathcal O_{X_\Omega})=\deg_{X_\Omega}(\mathcal L_\Omega)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. So $\deg_{X_\Omega}(\mathcal L_\Omega)>0$.
*(⇒), descent of the degree.* $X$ is proper over $k$ of dimension $1$, so [lem-pc-degree-base-change](1) gives $\deg_X(\mathcal L)=\deg_{X_\Omega}(\mathcal L_\Omega)>0$ by step 3.

*(⇐), the components over $\Omega$.* Assume $\deg_X(\mathcal L)>0$, and let $\Omega$, $X_\Omega$, $p$ be as in step 1. By [lem-pc-base-change-closure-components], with $r:=[\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X):k]\geq1$, $X_\Omega=X_1\amalg\cdots\amalg X_r$ with each $X_j$ an open and closed subscheme which is a proper smooth connected curve over $\Omega$, and $\mathcal L_j:=(p^*\mathcal L)|_{X_j}$ satisfies $r\deg_{X_j}(\mathcal L_j)=\deg_X(\mathcal L)>0$, so $\deg_{X_j}(\mathcal L_j)>0$ for every $j$. (When $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the hypothesis of the unit and of the Lean, $r=1$ and $X_\Omega$ is connected.)

source.place: unit sk-thm-picard-rr, proof, (G): 'deg is preserved by flat base change, and $X_{\bar k}$ is again a smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ with $H^0=\bar k$' (stated there under the standing hypothesis $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$); Lean: Modules.degree_pullback in isAmple_of_degree_pos (RiemannRoch.lean 1557-1578)

proof.text: *(⇐), the two degrees agree on each component.* Fix $j$ and let $g_j:=\dim_\Omega H^1(X_j,\mathcal O_{X_j})$ be the genus of the proper smooth connected curve $X_j$ [def-sc-genus]. By Riemann–Roch [lem-sc-riemann-roch](1), $\chi(X_j,\mathcal L_j)=\deg\mathcal L_j+1-g_j$ and $\chi(X_j,\mathcal O_{X_j})=1-g_j$, where $\deg\mathcal L_j$ is the degree of [def-sc-pic0]. Subtracting, $\deg\mathcal L_j=\chi(\mathcal L_j)-\chi(\mathcal O_{X_j})=\deg_{X_j}(\mathcal L_j)>0$ by step 5.

source.place: unit sk-thm-picard-rr, statement (RR): 'for every line bundle $\deg\cL=\chi(\cL)-\chi(\cO_X)$, i.e. the divisor degree agrees with the $\chi$-degree'

proof.text: *(⇐), a common very ample power.* Put $m:=\max_j(2g_j+1)\geq1$. For each $j$, $[\mathcal L_j^{\otimes m}]=m[\mathcal L_j]$ in the Picard group, whose law is $\otimes$ [def-sc-picard-group] [lem-sc-pic-group], and the degree of [def-sc-pic0] is a homomorphism, so $\deg(\mathcal L_j^{\otimes m})=m\deg\mathcal L_j\geq m\geq2g_j+1$ (step 6: $\deg\mathcal L_j\geq1$ is a positive integer). By [lem-sc-degree-2g1-very-ample] applied to the proper smooth connected curve $X_j$ of genus $g_j$ over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, $\mathcal L_j^{\otimes m}$ is very ample on $X_j$.

source.place: the choice m = 2g+1, Modules.degree_tensorPow and isVeryAmple_of_degree; here taken as the maximum over the components

proof.text: *(⇐), very ample over $\Omega$.* Pullback commutes with tensor products [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor], so $p^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})\cong(p^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes m}$, and its restriction to $X_j$ (the pullback along the open immersion $X_j\to X_\Omega$) is $\mathcal L_j^{\otimes m}$, very ample by step 7. $X_\Omega$ is proper over $\Omega$ (step 1), so [lem-pc-very-ample-disjoint-union] applied to the decomposition $X_\Omega=X_1\amalg\cdots\amalg X_r$ shows that $p^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ is very ample on $X_\Omega$.

source.place: hv.of_iso (Modules.nonempty_pullback_tensorPow_iso _ ℒ m); the decomposition into components is not in the Lean, which assumes H^0(X,O_X)=k

proof.text: *(⇐), descent.* $X$ is of finite type over $k$ and $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is invertible; its base change to $\Omega$ is very ample by step 8, so $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ is very ample on $X$ [lem-pc-very-ample-descends]. As $m\geq1$, $\mathcal L$ is ample [def-sc-ample].

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme which is smooth of relative
dimension $1$ and proper over $k$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=k$, and
$\mathcal{L}$ an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then $\mathcal{L}$ is ample if and
only if $\deg(\mathcal{L})>0$.

proof.text:
*Preliminaries.* $X$ is nonempty and connected, since
$H^0(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=k$ is a field and so has no nontrivial idempotents;
its local rings are regular ([lem-sc-smooth-regular]), hence domains, so
$X$ is integral, and it is one-dimensional. In particular $X$ is a curve
in the sense of [def-pc-dimension].

*($\Rightarrow$).* By [def-sc-ample], $\mathcal{L}$ ample implies
$\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}$ very ample for some $m\ge1$; fix such an $m$ and an
immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^N_k$ with
$\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}=i^*\mathcal{O}(1)$. Since $X$ is proper, the immersion is a
closed immersion (the image of the proper $X$ is closed, and an
immersion with closed image is a closed immersion; Schemes, Lemma
26.10.4, Tag [01IQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01IQ)).
Choose $x_0\in X$ and a section $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m})$ with
$s(x_0)\neq0$ (the base locus of a very ample module is empty: the
linear system $\mathbf P(H^0(X,\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}))$ gives the embedding,
so for every point there is a section not vanishing at it). The zero
scheme $D=Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor (finite closed
subscheme of the smooth curve; the local description of
[def-pc-zero-scheme] and the DVR structure of
[rem-pc-regularity-sc]: the ideal of $D$ at each of its points is
generated by a nonzero element of the DVR $\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$, hence
invertible) and finite (a closed subset of the curve of dimension $0$;
$X_s$ is a dense open of the curve, so $D$ is an effective Cartier
divisor of finite type and dimension $0$, hence finite). Moreover
$D\neq\emptyset$: if $D=\emptyset$, then $s$ is a nowhere vanishing
section, so $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}\cong\mathcal{O}_X$; but the trivial module is not
ample on a curve: if $\mathcal{O}_X$ were ample,
then by [def-sc-ample] some power is very ample, so a closed
immersion of $X$ into a projective space exists with an ample structure
sheaf: a nowhere vanishing module's powers have no sections separating
points; or directly: the affine open sets $X_s$ (for $s$ the constant
$1$) give $X\subseteq$ one affine piece, so $X$ would be affine, and
a proper affine scheme over $k$ is finite over $k$, but the curve is
one-dimensional): contradiction. Hence $\deg D\ge1$. From the exact
sequence $0\to\mathcal{O}_X\to\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}\to\mathcal Q\to0$ with
$\mathcal Q$ supported on $D$ and the computation
$\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal Q)=\deg D$ of [lem-pc-degree-base-change](2) (and
affineness/finiteness of $D$), the additivity of $\chi$ gives

$$
\chi(\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m})=\chi(\mathcal{O}_X)+\deg D,\qquad
\text{so}\qquad
m\deg(\mathcal{L})=\deg(\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m})=\deg D\ge1 ,
$$

and $\deg\mathcal{L}>0$.

*($\Leftarrow$).* Assume $\deg\mathcal{L}>0$. By
[lem-pc-degree-base-change](1), $\deg(\mathcal{L}_{\bar k})=\deg\mathcal{L}>0$,
and $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$ and proper over
$\bar k$ ([lem-pc-proper-base-change], [lem-pc-dim-base-change]), with
$H^0(X_{\bar k},\mathcal{O})=H^0(X,\mathcal{O})\otimes_k\bar k=\bar k$
([lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom]); by the preliminaries it is a
connected, hence integral, smooth proper curve over the algebraically
closed field $\bar k$, of genus $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$
([lem-pc-genus-base-change]). By [lem-sc-positive-degree-ample] the module
$\mathcal{L}_{\bar k}$ is ample.
Then $\mathcal{L}$ is ample: by [def-sc-ample] some power
$\mathcal{L}_{\bar k}^{\otimes m}$ is very ample, i.e. the base change of
$\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}$ to $\bar k$ is very ample; by
[lem-pc-very-ample-descends] $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}$ is very ample over
$k$, hence $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
